title: 1. What prompt engineering really is
body:
Prompt engineering is writing clear instructions so AI produces useful output: role, goal, context, constraints, format. Not magic spells.

Vague prompts get vague results. Specific prompts reduce guessing. You own what you send after editing.

Action: rewrite one recent AI prompt with role, success criteria, and format.

Apply "What prompt engineering really is" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 2. How models follow instructions
body:
Models predict likely text; they do not automatically know your business facts. They can sound confident while wrong.

Put critical rules early. Separate instructions from source documents. Never paste secrets into public tools.

Action: move your most important constraint to the first two lines of your best prompt.

Apply "How models follow instructions" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 3. Anatomy of a strong prompt
body:
Include role, task, context, constraints, optional examples, output format. Example: receptionist role, WhatsApp reply task, price facts, under 60 words, message only.

Action: build one skeleton prompt for your most common task.

Apply "Anatomy of a strong prompt" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 4. Role context constraints and format
body:
Role sets voice. Context supplies your facts. Constraints forbid bad behaviour. Format makes output paste-ready (WhatsApp, CSV, JSON).

Action: add a must-not list to your main prompt.

Apply "Role context constraints and format" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 5. Few-shot examples that work
body:
Show 1–5 input→output examples when format is picky. Keep examples consistent. Bad examples teach bad patterns.

Action: add one gold-standard example to a writing prompt.

Apply "Few-shot examples that work" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 6. Chain of thought and stepwise reasoning
body:
For multi-step problems ask for step-by-step work, then a clear final answer. Verify numbers and policies yourself.

Action: add 'list assumptions first' to one analysis prompt.

Apply "Chain of thought and stepwise reasoning" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 7. Prompting for business writing
body:
Name reader, desired action, facts, tone, max length. Generate variants, then a second pass to cut fluff. Always verify names and numbers.

Action: create a payment-follow-up email prompt with your real invoice fields as placeholders.

Apply "Prompting for business writing" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 8. Prompting for code and technical work
body:
Specify language, versions, I/O, errors, constraints. Ask for tests and what could break. Run all code yourself.

Action: paste one error message into a structured debug prompt template.

Apply "Prompting for code and technical work" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 9. Prompting for research and analysis
body:
Separate extract-from-source from advice. Require UNKNOWN when facts are missing. Define the decision you need.

Action: run a two-step prompt on a document you already trust.

Apply "Prompting for research and analysis" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 10. Iteration debugging and evals
body:
Change one variable at a time. Keep a scoreboard of 5–10 test cases. Stop random tinkering.

Action: write five test inputs for your main prompt.

Apply "Iteration debugging and evals" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 11. Safety privacy and hallucination control
body:
No passwords, OTPs, or full customer databases in public tools. Forbid invented statistics. Humans stay responsible for legal/medical/financial advice.

Action: add a privacy rule to your team AI guidelines.

Apply "Safety privacy and hallucination control" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.

title: 12. Building a personal prompt library
body:
Folder by Sales, Support, Content, Code. Store title, prompt, when to use, sample output. Version improvements. Review monthly.

Action: save your three best prompts in one note today.

Apply "Building a personal prompt library" this week: schedule one concrete action and complete it before the weekend.
